scenes.script:
PIKE: Dawson. Stand up.
KEISHA: In a minute, Mr. Pike.
PIKE: Not in a minute. Now. Mr. Randall is walking the store today. The regional inspection is today. And you are sitting on the floor in aisle seven.
KEISHA: This man's sugar dropped. The ambulance is nine minutes out.
PIKE: Then the ambulance will handle it. That is what they are for.
KEISHA: In nine minutes he can go under.
RANDALL: Douglas, what is the situation here?
PIKE: A customer incident. It is contained.

PIKE: That is an unpaid item, yes.
RANDALL: And the floor down there is still wet. I have it on my sheet.
PIKE: It will be corrected. Dawson, get up and get the cones.
KEISHA: Sir, I will get the cones the second the paramedics take him.
PIKE: You are refusing a direct instruction.

WALTER: Do not shout at her.

shots.text: [NHỊP] Toàn cảnh phòng nghỉ nhân viên: PIKE ngồi ghế trái bàn, tờ giấy in sẵn úp trước mặt, bút trong tay; KEISHA đứng bên phải bàn, còn nguyên đồng phục, không ngồi; đèn huỳnh quang, máy chấm công kêu tách

shots.text:
PIKE: Sit down.
KEISHA: I would rather stand.
PIKE: Sit down, Keisha.
KEISHA: Is he okay? Did anybody call the hospital?
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA tiền cảnh phải, máy cao · PIKE NÉT ngồi ghế trái bàn, ngước lên

shots.text: PIKE: That is not our business anymore. Once they load a customer, it is out of our hands. Do you know what today was?
shots.goc: OTS qua vai PIKE tiền cảnh trái · KEISHA NÉT đứng bên phải bàn, nhìn xuống Pike

shots.text:
KEISHA: The regional inspection.
PIKE: The regional inspection. One day a year. And Randall's report will say wet floor unattended, staff seated on the sales floor, unpaid merchandise consumed on the premises.
shots.goc: PIKE NÉT ngồi ghế trái bàn, đọc từng mục · KEISHA vai-gáy mờ rìa phải trên

shots.text: KEISHA: Consumed. He was shaking so hard he could not hold the bottle.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT đứng bên phải bàn, cúi nhìn Pike · PIKE mờ đỉnh đầu và vai rìa trái dưới

shots.text:
PIKE: I am reading you the categories. I did not invent the categories.
KEISHA: Take the bottle out of my check. It is three dollars and nineteen cents.
shots.goc: PIKE NÉT ngồi ghế trái bàn · KEISHA NÉT đứng bên phải bàn

shots.text: PIKE: It does not work like that. Once it is opened without payment, it is an event. It goes in the system as an event.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA tiền cảnh phải, máy cao · PIKE NÉT ngồi ghế trái bàn, ngón tay gõ lên tờ giấy

shots.text:
KEISHA: Say the word you mean.
PIKE: Theft of merchandise.
KEISHA: Six years, Mr. Pike. Six years I opened this store at five in the morning.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai PIKE tiền cảnh trái · KEISHA NÉT đứng bên phải bàn, mặt cứng lại

shots.text: PIKE: And in six years you have never given me a problem, which is why this is hard.
shots.goc: PIKE NÉT ngồi ghế trái bàn, ngước nhìn Keisha · KEISHA vai-gáy mờ rìa phải trên

shots.text:
KEISHA: This is not hard for you. You already printed the paper. It is in your hand.
PIKE: Termination for theft of merchandise and abandonment of post. Sign at the bottom.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT đứng bên phải bàn, nhìn xuống tờ giấy · PIKE NÉT ngồi ghế trái bàn, cầm tờ giấy đọc

shots.text:
KEISHA: And my reference letter?
PIKE: I cannot write a letter with this on the file.
KEISHA: Denise. You saw him on the floor. Say something.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai PIKE tiền cảnh trái · KEISHA NÉT đứng bên phải bàn, quay đầu về phía cửa gọi Denise · DENISE NÉT xa ở cửa hé phía sau bên phải

shots.text:
DENISE: Keisha —
PIKE: Denise, go back to register four.
DENISE: I am sorry.
shots.goc: DENISE NÉT ở cửa hé phía sau bên phải, mắt ướt · KEISHA nửa mặt mờ tiền cảnh phải, ngoái về cửa · PIKE vai mờ rìa trái

shots.text: [NHỊP] KEISHA cúi người xuống bàn, cầm bút ký vào cuối tờ giấy sa thải; PIKE ngồi nhìn, không nói; tiếng bút sột soạt, tiếng máy chấm công
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT cúi người xuống bàn bên phải, ký · PIKE NÉT ngồi ghế trái bàn, mờ hơn phía sau

scenes.script:
PIKE: Sit down.
KEISHA: I would rather stand.
PIKE: Sit down, Keisha.
KEISHA: Is he okay? Did anybody call the hospital?
PIKE: That is not our business anymore. Once they load a customer, it is out of our hands. Do you know what today was?
KEISHA: The regional inspection.
PIKE: The regional inspection. One day a year. And Randall's report will say wet floor unattended, staff seated on the sales floor, unpaid merchandise consumed on the premises.
KEISHA: Consumed. He was shaking so hard he could not hold the bottle.
PIKE: I am reading you the categories. I did not invent the categories.
KEISHA: Take the bottle out of my check. It is three dollars and nineteen cents.
PIKE: It does not work like that. Once it is opened without payment, it is an event. It goes in the system as an event.
KEISHA: Say the word you mean.
PIKE: Theft of merchandise.
KEISHA: Six years, Mr. Pike. Six years I opened this store at five in the morning.
PIKE: And in six years you have never given me a problem, which is why this is hard.
KEISHA: This is not hard for you. You already printed the paper. It is in your hand.
PIKE: Termination for theft of merchandise and abandonment of post. Sign at the bottom.
KEISHA: And my reference letter?
PIKE: I cannot write a letter with this on the file.
KEISHA: Denise. You saw him on the floor. Say something.
DENISE: Keisha —
PIKE: Denise, go back to register four.
DENISE: I am sorry.
KEISHA: Give me the pen.

shots.text:
DENISE: Keisha. Keisha, wait.
KEISHA: I am fine, Denise.
DENISE: Take this.
KEISHA: No.

KEISHA: Keep your money.
DENISE: I should have said something in there. I opened my mouth and nothing came out.

shots.text:

DENISE: My son starts school in September. If Pike puts one thing on my file —

shots.text:

DENISE: What are you going to tell your mother?

LORETTA: And you opened it anyway.
KEISHA: His hands were shaking, Mama. He was going to go under on the floor and forty people walked past him with their carts.
LORETTA: I am not scolding you.
KEISHA: It sounds like scolding.
LORETTA: I am telling you I taught you those three things so you would come home safe. And you went and became a person who breaks the third one for a stranger. I do not know whether to be proud or sick.
KEISHA: Can you be both?
LORETTA: I am both.

shots.text:
PHARMACIST: Dawson. Two prescriptions. The metformin and the heart medication.

shots.text:
PHARMACIST: I am sorry. The system already dropped you.

shots.goc: PHARMACIST NÉT đứng sau quầy trái · KEISHA NÉT đứng trước quầy phải, cả hai rõ mặt

shots.text: KEISHA: I know what happens if she runs out. I am asking which one I can leave here for eleven days without her ending up in an emergency room.

shots.text:
RECRUITER: Six years at one employer. That looks good. Employers like that.

shots.text:
RECRUITER: And you left in March?

shots.goc: RECRUITER NÉT ngồi sau bàn trái · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách phải, cả hai rõ mặt

shots.text:
RECRUITER: I am asking you to say it.
KEISHA: Theft of merchandise. A three dollar bottle of orange juice that I opened for a man having a diabetic emergency in my aisle.

RECRUITER: That is a good story.

RECRUITER: I believe you. I want you to hear me. I believe you. But I place people in hospitals, schools and warehouses.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA tiền cảnh phải · RECRUITER NÉT ngồi sau bàn trái

shots.text: RECRUITER: Every one of those clients runs a background screen, and the screen does not have a box for the reason. It has a box for the word.

shots.text:

shots.text:

shots.goc: OTS qua vai RECRUITER tiền cảnh trái · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách phải

shots.text:
RECRUITER: Then I have residential cleaning. Cash, no screen, no benefits. Eleven dollars an hour.

KEISHA: It is in the file you are reading.
RECRUITER: I am asking you to say it.
KEISHA: Theft of merchandise. A three dollar bottle of orange juice that I opened for a man having a diabetic emergency in my aisle.
RECRUITER: That is a good story.
KEISHA: It is not a story.
RECRUITER: I believe you. I want you to hear me. I believe you. But I place people in hospitals, schools and warehouses. Every one of those clients runs a background screen, and the screen does not have a box for the reason. It has a box for the word.
KEISHA: And the word is theft.
RECRUITER: The word is theft.
KEISHA: So what do I do?
RECRUITER: Honestly? You wait two years and the word gets old. Or you get your old employer to amend the record.
KEISHA: He will not.
RECRUITER: Then I have residential cleaning. Cash, no screen, no benefits. Eleven dollars an hour.
KEISHA: I was making sixteen.
RECRUITER: I know.
KEISHA: Put my name down for it.

shots.text: [NHỊP] Bếp đêm dưới đèn trần vàng: LORETTA ngồi đầu bàn, hai lọ thuốc đặt trước mặt; KEISHA ngồi đối diện, ôm ly nước, chưa ai nói

shots.text:
LORETTA: You took the heart pills and left my sugar ones.
KEISHA: I did not.
LORETTA: Keisha, I counted the bottles.
KEISHA: I am getting yours on the fifteenth.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA tiền cảnh trái · LORETTA NÉT ngồi ghế đầu bàn phải

shots.text:
LORETTA: Today is the fourth.
KEISHA: Then I am getting it on the fifteenth, Mama.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai LORETTA tiền cảnh phải · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế đối diện trái

shots.text:
LORETTA: This is what I was afraid of. This exact thing. This is why I did not want you to leave school.
KEISHA: We are not doing that tonight.
shots.goc: LORETTA NÉT ngồi ghế đầu bàn phải · KEISHA vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh trái

shots.text:
LORETTA: Two semesters. You had two semesters left.
KEISHA: You could not walk to the bathroom by yourself that year.
LORETTA: I know what I could not do.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai LORETTA tiền cảnh phải · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế đối diện trái

shots.text:
LORETTA: I lay in that bed and listened to my daughter give up a degree for me and I said nothing, because I needed her.
KEISHA: You needed me. So I came.
shots.goc: LORETTA NÉT ngồi ghế đầu bàn phải · KEISHA vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh trái

shots.text:
LORETTA: And now you are thirty-one and a store took your name for three dollars.
KEISHA: Mama.
LORETTA: What.
shots.goc: LORETTA NÉT ngồi ghế đầu bàn phải · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế đối diện trái, cả hai rõ mặt dưới đèn

shots.text:
KEISHA: Can I say something ugly?
LORETTA: Say it.
KEISHA: I keep waiting to feel sorry that I opened that bottle. And I do not.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế đối diện trái · LORETTA vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh phải

shots.text: [NHỊP] Hai mẹ con ngồi im dưới đèn bếp; LORETTA đặt tay lên mu bàn tay Keisha giữa bàn, hai lọ thuốc bên cạnh, không ai nói
shots.goc: LORETTA NÉT ngồi ghế đầu bàn phải · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế đối diện trái, cả hai cúi nhìn tay

shots.text:
KEISHA: I have gone over it maybe four hundred times and every time I open it again.
LORETTA: That is not ugly.
KEISHA: The ugly part is the next thing.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA tiền cảnh trái · LORETTA NÉT ngồi ghế đầu bàn phải

shots.text: KEISHA: If doing the right thing costs everything, every single time, then what is the point of being the kind of person you raised?
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế đối diện trái · LORETTA vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh phải

shots.text:
LORETTA: I do not have an answer for that tonight.
KEISHA: That is okay.
LORETTA: Sit here with me anyway.
shots.goc: LORETTA NÉT ngồi ghế đầu bàn phải · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế đối diện trái, cả hai rõ mặt dưới đèn
shots.notes: KẾT CLIP: KEISHA nhấc người định đứng dậy rồi ngồi lại; hai tay buông xuống bàn.

scenes.script:
LORETTA: You took the heart pills and left my sugar ones.
KEISHA: I did not.
LORETTA: Keisha, I counted the bottles.
KEISHA: I am getting yours on the fifteenth.
LORETTA: Today is the fourth.
KEISHA: Then I am getting it on the fifteenth, Mama.
LORETTA: This is what I was afraid of. This exact thing. This is why I did not want you to leave school.
KEISHA: We are not doing that tonight.
LORETTA: Two semesters. You had two semesters left.
KEISHA: You could not walk to the bathroom by yourself that year.
LORETTA: I know what I could not do. I lay in that bed and listened to my daughter give up a degree for me and I said nothing, because I needed her.
KEISHA: You needed me. So I came.
LORETTA: And now you are thirty-one and a store took your name for three dollars.
KEISHA: Mama.
LORETTA: What.
KEISHA: Can I say something ugly?
LORETTA: Say it.
KEISHA: I keep waiting to feel sorry that I opened that bottle. And I do not. I have gone over it maybe four hundred times and every time I open it again.
LORETTA: That is not ugly.
KEISHA: The ugly part is the next thing. If doing the right thing costs everything, every single time, then what is the point of being the kind of person you raised?
LORETTA: I do not have an answer for that tonight.
KEISHA: That is okay.
LORETTA: Sit here with me anyway.

shots.text:
LORETTA: There is tea. It is not fancy.

WALTER: I came to say thank you, and to ask a question.
KEISHA: Ask it.
WALTER: Why did you stop?

shots.text: WALTER: A serious one. Forty people went by. Every one of them saw me. Why did you stop?

shots.text:
KEISHA: Because you said the eggs.
WALTER: The eggs.
KEISHA: You were half gone and the thing you were worried about was paying for eggs. My mother does that.

shots.text: KEISHA: When her sugar drops she starts apologizing to people who are not in the room. So I knew what I was looking at.

shots.text:
WALTER: You knew because you have seen it at this table.
KEISHA: Twice.
WALTER: Miss Dawson, I should tell you my full name.
KEISHA: Walter is fine.
shots.goc: WALTER NÉT ngồi ghế khách giữa, nghiêng người sang trái · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế trái cạnh cửa sổ · LORETTA vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh phải

shots.text:

shots.text:
WALTER: Gray like the sign. I opened the first one in nineteen eighty-four. Two aisles and a walk-in cooler.
KEISHA: I have mopped under your name for six years.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai LORETTA tiền cảnh phải · WALTER NÉT ngồi ghế khách giữa · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế trái cạnh cửa sổ, xa hơn

shots.text:
WALTER: And on Tuesday my name fired you for three dollars.
KEISHA: You know about that.
WALTER: Payroll sent me the file this morning. I read the sentence they wrote about you.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA tiền cảnh trái · WALTER NÉT ngồi ghế khách giữa, mặt trầm xuống

shots.text: WALTER: Then I read it again, because I did not believe a company I built would put that word next to what you did.

shots.text:
KEISHA: The word is theft.
WALTER: I know what the word is. I am ashamed of it.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế trái cạnh cửa sổ, nói khẽ · WALTER NÉT ngồi ghế khách giữa, quay sang cô · LORETTA mờ hậu cảnh phải

shots.text: [NHỊP] Im lặng sau "I am ashamed of it.": cận chai nước cam còn kín đứng giữa bàn cạnh ba tách trà, không ai chạm; máy lia lên mặt KEISHA nhìn WALTER cúi đầu, LORETTA khẽ đặt tay lên bàn
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế trái cạnh cửa sổ · WALTER NÉT ngồi ghế khách giữa, cúi đầu · LORETTA mờ phải

scenes.script:
LORETTA: There is tea. It is not fancy.
WALTER: Tea is exactly right.
LORETTA: You came a long way to return a bottle of juice.
WALTER: I came to say thank you, and to ask a question.
KEISHA: Ask it.
WALTER: Why did you stop?
KEISHA: What kind of question is that?
WALTER: A serious one. Forty people went by. Every one of them saw me. Why did you stop?
KEISHA: Because you said the eggs.
WALTER: The eggs.
KEISHA: You were half gone and the thing you were worried about was paying for eggs. My mother does that. When her sugar drops she starts apologizing to people who are not in the room. So I knew what I was looking at.
WALTER: You knew because you have seen it at this table.
KEISHA: Twice.
WALTER: Miss Dawson, I should tell you my full name.
KEISHA: Walter is fine.
WALTER: Walter Gray.
KEISHA: Say that again.
WALTER: Walter Gray.
LORETTA: Gray like the sign?
WALTER: Gray like the sign. I opened the first one in nineteen eighty-four. Two aisles and a walk-in cooler.
KEISHA: I have mopped under your name for six years.
WALTER: And on Tuesday my name fired you for three dollars.
KEISHA: You know about that.
WALTER: Payroll sent me the file this morning. I read the sentence they wrote about you. Then I read it again, because I did not believe a company I built would put that word next to what you did.
KEISHA: The word is theft.
WALTER: I know what the word is. I am ashamed of it.

shots.text:
KEISHA: This is a big building for a retired man.
WALTER: They keep the office for me so I feel useful. I sit in it about once a month.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA đứng, tiền cảnh phải · WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn gỗ bên trái, cười nhẹ

shots.text:
WALTER: Sit down, Miss Dawson.
KEISHA: Keisha is fine.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai WALTER tiền cảnh trái · KEISHA NÉT đứng trước ghế khách bên phải, tay đặt lên lưng ghế

shots.text:
WALTER: Keisha. I asked you here because I want to offer you something, and I want to be careful how I say it.
KEISHA: Say it plain.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách bên phải · WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn bên trái, chọn chữ

shots.text: WALTER: We run a program called the Store Operations Fellowship. Six months. Full salary. At the end you either get a store leadership post or you do not.
shots.goc: WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn bên trái, nói chậm · KEISHA vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh phải

shots.text:
KEISHA: No.
WALTER: You have not heard the terms.
KEISHA: I do not need the terms. No.
WALTER: Why?
shots.goc: OTS qua vai WALTER tiền cảnh trái · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách bên phải, mặt không đổi

shots.text:
KEISHA: Because I gave you a juice.
WALTER: That is not the only reason you are in this room.
KEISHA: It is the reason you know my name.
WALTER: True.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA tiền cảnh phải · WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn bên trái

shots.text:
KEISHA: Mr. Gray, if I take a job because I was kind to you, then everything I did on that floor turns into a transaction. And it was not one.
WALTER: I understand.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách bên phải, nhìn thẳng ông · WALTER vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh trái

shots.text: KEISHA: I do not think you do. Where I come from, when somebody rich hands you something, you spend the rest of your life being told you did not earn it.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách bên phải, mặt nghiêng 3/4 · WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn bên trái, lắng nghe

shots.text: WALTER: Then earn it. There is an assessment. Ninety minutes, written, scored blind. There were two hundred and six applicants last cycle and thirty-one got in.
shots.goc: WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn bên trái, dứt khoát · KEISHA vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh phải

shots.text:
WALTER: I cannot score it for you and I would not.
KEISHA: And my file? The word on my file?
WALTER: I cannot delete it.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai WALTER tiền cảnh trái · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách bên phải, hỏi về hồ sơ

shots.text: WALTER: Legally I cannot, and honestly I would not want the company to be the kind of place where one phone call erases a record.
shots.goc: WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn bên trái, nói thẳng thắn · KEISHA vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh phải

shots.text:
KEISHA: So it follows me in.
WALTER: It follows you in. Which means the people in that program will look at you sideways from day one.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách bên phải · WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn bên trái

shots.text:
KEISHA: Then what exactly are you giving me?
WALTER: A door. Not a chair. The door, and nothing on the other side of it but work.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA tiền cảnh phải · WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn bên trái

shots.text: KEISHA: Where do I sign for the test?
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách bên phải, khoé miệng nhếch · WALTER vai-gáy mờ tiền cảnh trái

shots.text: [NHỊP] WALTER mở ngăn kéo lấy một tờ đăng ký thi, đẩy chậm qua mặt bàn về phía KEISHA; cô nhìn tờ giấy rồi đặt tay lên nó
shots.goc: WALTER NÉT ngồi sau bàn bên trái, đẩy tờ giấy qua bàn · KEISHA NÉT ngồi ghế khách bên phải, đặt tay lên tờ giấy

scenes.script:
KEISHA: This is a big building for a retired man.
WALTER: They keep the office for me so I feel useful. I sit in it about once a month. Sit down, Miss Dawson.
KEISHA: Keisha is fine.
WALTER: Keisha. I asked you here because I want to offer you something, and I want to be careful how I say it.
KEISHA: Say it plain.
WALTER: We run a program called the Store Operations Fellowship. Six months. Full salary. At the end you either get a store leadership post or you do not.
KEISHA: No.
WALTER: You have not heard the terms.
KEISHA: I do not need the terms. No.
WALTER: Why?
KEISHA: Because I gave you a juice.
WALTER: That is not the only reason you are in this room.
KEISHA: It is the reason you know my name.
WALTER: True.
KEISHA: Mr. Gray, if I take a job because I was kind to you, then everything I did on that floor turns into a transaction. And it was not one.
WALTER: I understand.
KEISHA: I do not think you do. Where I come from, when somebody rich hands you something, you spend the rest of your life being told you did not earn it.
WALTER: Then earn it. There is an assessment. Ninety minutes, written, scored blind. There were two hundred and six applicants last cycle and thirty-one got in. I cannot score it for you and I would not.
KEISHA: And my file? The word on my file?
WALTER: I cannot delete it. Legally I cannot, and honestly I would not want the company to be the kind of place where one phone call erases a record.
KEISHA: So it follows me in.
WALTER: It follows you in. Which means the people in that program will look at you sideways from day one.
KEISHA: Then what exactly are you giving me?
WALTER: A door. Not a chair. The door, and nothing on the other side of it but work.
KEISHA: Where do I sign for the test?

scenes.script:
ELAINE: This is your assigned store. Ninety-one years old neighborhood, median customer age is sixty-eight. It is our worst performer in the region. Tell me what you see.
COLIN: Foot traffic is fine. Basket size is the problem. People are coming in and buying four items.
ELAINE: Miss Dawson?
KEISHA: Can I walk it first?
ELAINE: Take ten minutes.
KEISHA: I do not need ten. Look at the floor by the dairy case.
COLIN: It is a floor.
KEISHA: It is a floor that has been mopped and re-mopped in the same three-foot patch until the finish is worn off. That is a leak somebody has been wiping for two years instead of fixing. That patch is where people slip.
ELAINE: Go on.
KEISHA: Top shelf, aisle four. The tea, the flour, the big detergent. All of it at six feet in a store where the average customer is sixty-eight years old.
COLIN: Planograms are set nationally.
KEISHA: I know. I have loaded them. And every single day somebody's grandmother stands in aisle four waiting for a stock boy, and if nobody comes in two minutes she leaves the tea and walks out. That is your basket size.
COLIN: That is anecdote, not data.
KEISHA: Then here is data. There is one bench in this store. It is by the restroom, and it is broken. There is nowhere to sit down in a forty thousand square foot building.
ELAINE: Why does that matter?
KEISHA: Because a customer who cannot sit down shops for eleven minutes. A customer who can sit down for ninety seconds shops for twenty-five.
COLIN: Where did you get those numbers?
KEISHA: From six years of watching people give up.

scenes.script:
LORETTA: It is two o'clock.
KEISHA: I know. Go back to bed, Mama.
LORETTA: What is all this paper?
KEISHA: Incident reports. Three years of them, from six stores.
LORETTA: And you are reading every one.
KEISHA: There are four hundred and ten.
LORETTA: Keisha.
KEISHA: Colin said anecdote, not data. So I am going to walk into that room with data.
LORETTA: You are going to walk into that room with no sleep.
KEISHA: Mama, sit down a second. Can I ask you something?
LORETTA: Ask.
KEISHA: There are people in that program with master's degrees. Colin knows words I have to look up on my phone under the table. Yesterday a man asked me about shrink allocation and I had to say I did not know what that meant, out loud, in front of nine people.
LORETTA: And?
KEISHA: And nobody laughed. Which was worse. They just waited for me to catch up.
LORETTA: What is the question, baby?
KEISHA: What if I am not smart. What if I am just somebody who was standing in the right aisle.
LORETTA: Bring that lamp closer.
KEISHA: Why?
LORETTA: Because if we are going to read four hundred and ten reports, I am not doing it in the dark. Give me half the stack.

shots.goc: toàn cảnh từ cửa · KEISHA NÉT ngồi bên phải bàn nhìn sang Colin · COLIN NÉT ngồi bên trái bàn nhìn lại · ELAINE ngồi đầu bàn giữa

scenes.script:
ELAINE: Ten weeks. Read the numbers.
KEISHA: Across the six pilot stores. Customer incidents down sixty-two percent. Assisted retrieval calls down seventy-eight percent. Average transaction size up four dollars and eleven cents. Trips per customer per month up from two point one to two point eight.
ELAINE: And the age band?
KEISHA: Customers over sixty-five are up nine percent in visits. That is the group everybody said was leaving us for delivery.
ELAINE: Mr. Marsh, you were the loudest voice against this. Your response.
COLIN: The numbers are real. I checked them myself.
ELAINE: That is not a response.
COLIN: My response is that this should scale to the whole southern region, and I would like to be on the team that does it.
ELAINE: Noted. Anything else?
COLIN: Yes. Dawson, can I say this in the room or do you want it in the hall?
KEISHA: Say it in the room.
COLIN: I have been in this company for eight years and I have never once been the person who noticed something. I optimize things other people noticed. You walked into a store I have visited nine times and saw a wet patch on the floor.
KEISHA: You checked my numbers line by line, on your own time, to try to prove me wrong.
COLIN: Yes.
KEISHA: That is also noticing. That is the part I am bad at.
ELAINE: Then here is the decision. Reach and Rest goes to forty stores in the southern region. Dawson leads. Marsh runs the rollout schedule. Board presentation is in three weeks. Do not embarrass me.

shots.text: [NHỊP] Keisha khép bìa hồ sơ, đứng yên; Board Member đặt bút xuống, Elaine nhìn cha mình không có ở đó — nhìn Keisha một giây rồi gật rất khẽ.
shots.goc: KEISHA đứng đầu bàn bên phải khép bìa hồ sơ, rõ mặt · BOARD MEMBER và ELAINE ngồi dãy trái CẢ HAI RÕ MẶT nhìn nhau

scenes.script:
ELAINE: Board members, this is Keisha Dawson. She will present the Reach and Rest results and the forty store proposal.
KEISHA: Before I start, I need to correct my own deck.
BOARD MEMBER: Correct it how?
KEISHA: The number you have in front of you says incidents fell sixty-two percent. That number is wrong. The correct figure is forty-one percent.
BOARD MEMBER: When did you find this?
KEISHA: Two nights ago. Twenty-two events at two stores were re-classified from incident to near miss during the pilot window. I have the audit trail, the login, and the date. It is in the folder behind the tab marked correction.
BOARD MEMBER: Did you do the re-classification?
KEISHA: No.
BOARD MEMBER: Do you know who did?
KEISHA: I do, and I have put it in writing to the audit office. I am not going to say the name in this room before they have finished, because I could be wrong about why it was done.
ELAINE: What are you asking us for?
KEISHA: Same thing as before. Forty stores. On forty-one percent instead of sixty-two.
BOARD MEMBER: Forty-one is still the best safety result this company has had in nine years.
ELAINE: Miss Dawson. One question, and I want a short answer. You could have said nothing. Nobody in this building had found it. Why did you bring it in here yourself?
KEISHA: Because if a wrong number stays in the file, in three years somebody puts a bench in the wrong place and an old man goes down in aisle seven and nobody stops.
ELAINE: That is your answer?
KEISHA: That is the whole answer.

shots.text: [NHỊP] Căng-tin 1 giờ 30 chiều thưa người, nắng qua cửa kính. Keisha ngồi một mình bàn cạnh cửa sổ, khay bánh mì gà chưa động tới; Colin bước vào từ lối vào, đi thẳng tới bàn cô.
shots.goc: toàn cảnh rộng căng-tin · KEISHA ngồi bàn cạnh cửa sổ bên phải, nhỏ trong khung · COLIN đang bước tới từ lối vào bên trái, rõ dáng

shots.text:
COLIN: You are not eating that.
KEISHA: I have been sitting here forty minutes.
COLIN: The audit closed this morning.
KEISHA: I heard.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi bên phải ngẩng nhìn lên · COLIN đứng cạnh bàn bên trái RÕ MẶT, tay đặt lưng ghế

shots.text: COLIN: Pike is out of the region. They offered him a single store in the north and he took it. And I got a letter in my file.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai KEISHA tiền cảnh phải · COLIN NÉT ngồi đối diện bên trái

shots.text:
KEISHA: For what?
COLIN: I signed off on the week four data set without opening the underlying records. That is my job and I did not do it.
shots.goc: OTS qua vai COLIN tiền cảnh trái · KEISHA NÉT ngồi bên phải

shots.text:
COLIN: I did not do it because the number was good and a good number was convenient for me.
KEISHA: How long does the letter stay?
shots.goc: COLIN NÉT ngồi bên trái · KEISHA vai-gáy tiền cảnh phải (OTS qua vai KEISHA)

shots.text:
COLIN: Eighteen months. No promotion track, no leadership post.
KEISHA: So the rollout team.
shots.goc: COLIN bên trái và KEISHA bên phải CẢ HAI RÕ MẶT nghiêng

shots.text:
COLIN: I am off it. Effective yesterday. I came down here to tell you before you heard it from Elaine.
KEISHA: Colin. Have you eaten today?
shots.goc: COLIN NÉT ngồi bên trái · KEISHA vai-gáy tiền cảnh phải (OTS qua vai KEISHA)

shots.text:
COLIN: Why?
KEISHA: Because it is one thirty and you look like a man who has not.
COLIN: I am fine.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi bên phải · COLIN vai-gáy tiền cảnh trái (OTS qua vai COLIN)

shots.text: KEISHA: Take half of this. It is a chicken sandwich, it is not a favor.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi bên phải, tay đặt lên bánh mì · COLIN ngồi bên trái RÕ MẶT

shots.text: COLIN: After I stood up in a room and called you a nice story, you are handing me a sandwich.
shots.goc: COLIN NÉT ngồi bên trái nhìn xuống nửa bánh mì · KEISHA vai-gáy tiền cảnh phải (OTS qua vai KEISHA)

shots.text:
KEISHA: I am also going to ask Elaine to put you back on the rollout.
COLIN: You are not serious.
KEISHA: Forty stores in nine weeks.
shots.goc: KEISHA bên phải và COLIN bên trái CẢ HAI RÕ MẶT nghiêng

shots.text: KEISHA: There is exactly one person in this company who can build that schedule and he is sitting in front of me with a letter in his file.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi bên phải · COLIN vai-gáy tiền cảnh trái (OTS qua vai COLIN)

shots.text:
COLIN: She will say no.
KEISHA: Probably. Then I will ask again in a month.
COLIN: Why?
shots.goc: COLIN NÉT ngồi bên trái · KEISHA vai-gáy tiền cảnh phải (OTS qua vai KEISHA)

shots.text: KEISHA: Because you checked my numbers when you wanted me to fail, and you told me the truth about the eighteen months when you could have let me find out.
shots.goc: KEISHA NÉT ngồi bên phải · COLIN vai-gáy tiền cảnh trái (OTS qua vai COLIN)

shots.text: KEISHA: That is two things. Most people do not give me two.
shots.goc: KEISHA bên phải và COLIN bên trái CẢ HAI RÕ MẶT nghiêng

shots.text: [NHỊP] Colin cầm nửa bánh mì lên cắn một miếng, nhai chậm; Keisha cầm nửa còn lại, cuối cùng cũng ăn. Nắng chiều qua cửa kính, không ai nói gì.
shots.goc: COLIN ngồi bên trái cắn nửa bánh mì · KEISHA ngồi bên phải cầm nửa còn lại, CẢ HAI RÕ MẶT

scenes.script:
COLIN: You are not eating that.
KEISHA: I have been sitting here forty minutes.
COLIN: The audit closed this morning.
KEISHA: I heard.
COLIN: Pike is out of the region. They offered him a single store in the north and he took it. And I got a letter in my file.
KEISHA: For what?
COLIN: I signed off on the week four data set without opening the underlying records. That is my job and I did not do it. I did not do it because the number was good and a good number was convenient for me.
KEISHA: How long does the letter stay?
COLIN: Eighteen months. No promotion track, no leadership post.
KEISHA: So the rollout team.
COLIN: I am off it. Effective yesterday. I came down here to tell you before you heard it from Elaine.
KEISHA: Colin. Have you eaten today?
COLIN: Why?
KEISHA: Because it is one thirty and you look like a man who has not.
COLIN: I am fine.
KEISHA: Take half of this. It is a chicken sandwich, it is not a favor.
COLIN: After I stood up in a room and called you a nice story, you are handing me a sandwich.
KEISHA: I am also going to ask Elaine to put you back on the rollout.
COLIN: You are not serious.
KEISHA: Forty stores in nine weeks. There is exactly one person in this company who can build that schedule and he is sitting in front of me with a letter in his file.
COLIN: She will say no.
KEISHA: Probably. Then I will ask again in a month.
COLIN: Why?
KEISHA: Because you checked my numbers when you wanted me to fail, and you told me the truth about the eighteen months when you could have let me find out. That is two things. Most people do not give me two.
